pr_title: WebGLCubeUVMaps: Add support for render targets.
pr_body:
Fixed #22236.

**Description**

This PR adds support for render targets in `WebGLCubeUVMaps`. That means the render targets of cube cameras can now be used with PBR materials.

@elalish I've have enhanced `PMREMGenerator` such that it is possible to reuse existing render targets for the conversion process. I'm not sure how to implement the details of https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/issues/22236#issuecomment-948069315 though. 

TBH, it surprised me that the conversion per frame has such a decent performance (tested with `webgl_materials_cubemap_dynamic` and PBR materials). I had this different in mind when testing last year.
pr_comments:
@Mugen87 So far, this appears to be working for me.

`renderer.info` shows more shaders, but I expect that is just the non-disposed PMREM shaders.

> I've have enhanced PMREMGenerator such that it is possible to reuse existing render targets

It appears that is appropriate now, since the PMREM render target always has the same parameters regardless of the inputs.

>TBH, it surprised me that the conversion per frame has such a decent performance

Me, too. Perhaps you should also compare with a _cube_ environment map just in case.

In fact the `ms/frame` PMREM performance statistics would be of interest. 😇

Wow, I'm  impressed the performance  is decent for a PMREM per frame too! I mean, I did try to make it as fast as I could, and it may well be that converting  to halfFloats sped it  up significantly. I too would love to see some frame rate comparisons. 

My comment was about bringing  back the old mipmaps-as-PMREM solution that was in three.js before my PMREMGenerator and was removed during @WestLangley's simplification. However, if this is adequately fast, then perhaps there's no need. Would be good to test a WebXR example with lighting estimation as well.
@Mugen87 Should I merge this so we have some time to test performance?

>bringing back the old mipmaps-as-PMREM solution that was in three.js

@elalish Yes, that is what #23144 is about -- just in case it is needed as a fall-back.

> @Mugen87 Should I merge this so we have some time to test performance?

Yes, that sounds good. We still need to fix the WebXR example with lighting estimation.
Thanks!
@mrdoob build required
Done 👍
@Mugen87 Do the reflections look correct in your test cases?
After a closer look, it seems the reflections along the x axis are flipped. Let me file a PR to fix this issue.
@Mugen87 any plans for a sample to share?
In #23158, I've updated `webgl_materials_cubemap_dynamic.html` to use `MeshStandardMaterial`.

I tested my page, and the performance is quite ok. I found there still is a framebuffer of `_pingPongRenderTarget` in `PMREMGenerator`, which updates in each frame.  After running a few minutes, the framebuffer has been created and destoryed thousands of times. I think it's not necessary and can be optimized. 
BTW, I also want to pass the rendertarget parameters to the `.fromScene`, in this way I can update a pmrem texture in each frame under my control. should the PMREMGenerator support better for the situation of updating textures in each frame.
@Mugen87 Yes, that sounds  good to me. @WestLangley I believe those shaders all get disposed when the `dispose` method is called on PMREMGenerator, which seems reasonable.

@Mugen87 Do you think if it's ok about adding a extra parameter to `.fromScene`? https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/dev/src/extras/PMREMGenerator.js#L103 .  In this way the method can be used by a user controlled renderTarget.

@Mugen87 @elalish  `PMREMGenerator.dispose()` is not being called. We used to do that at the app level.

Granted, we do not want to dispose() if PMREM is generated every frame, but that is not the typical use case.

> PMREMGenerator.dispose() is not being called.

It is called in `WebGLRenderer.dispose()`. 

`WebGLCubeUVMaps` only creates a single instance of `PMREMGenerator`. Buffering certain resources for the conversion process (3 materials and 1 render target) within the renderer is the only solution. It's important to ensure that we don't create these entities over and over again.

> Do you think if it's ok about adding a extra parameter to .fromScene? https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/dev/src/extras/PMREMGenerator.js#L103 . In this way the method can be used by a user controlled renderTarget.

I'm not sure about the dimensions but other render target parameters should not be configurable by the user, IMO.

> I'm not sure about the dimensions but other render target parameters should not be configurable by the user, IMO.

@Mugen87 OK, thanks! Maybe my use case is not very common. Generating a realtime enviroment map can use CubeCamera now. I just guess using `.fromScene` can also implement the effect in example https://threejs.org/examples/webgl_materials_cubemap_dynamic.html , and maybe `fromScene` has a better performance with an outer render target. I tested the two different ways on two macbooks, and got the different results.

issue_context.title: WebGLRenderer: fails to convert CubeCamera renderTarget to PMREM CubeUV format
comments:
I did not honor this use case in #22178 because I could not figure out how to distinct between the render target of a cube camera and the render target of manually generated PMREM (on app level). Hence `WebGLCubeUVMaps` does not support textures of render targets in general. The respective line is:

https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/9b1faf830f09957f8ea4886985dbbef99fd81949/src/renderers/webgl/WebGLCubeUVMaps.js#L12
Besides, are you sure you want to regenerate the PMREM for a dynamic cube camera per frame?

This has to be fixed. Physical materials can only be rendered correctly with PMREM CubeUV maps. See https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/22178#issuecomment-887950445.

> I could not figure out how to distinct between the render target of a cube camera and the render target of manually generated PMREM (on app level).

There should no longer be manually-generated PMREMS, in theory. But given they still exist, maybe `CubeCamera` and/or `PMREMGenerator` can set a flag.

>Besides, are you sure you want to regenerate the PMREM for a dynamic cube camera per frame?

That is an edge case, and cannot be a reason to get this right.

> and cannot be a reason to get this right.

Oh, I did not want to use this an argument against the feature. But when it's implemented we have to document that dynamic cube cameras will be unusable (performance-wise) with a PBR material if PMREMs are generated internally each frame.

> But given they still exist, maybe CubeCamera and/or PMREMGenerator can set a flag.

Yes, some sort of flag could be the solution. A key problem is to detect when a render target is considered to be ready for PMREM processing. It's easy to detect this for normal textures but not for render targets.

The texture is the render target of a cube camera if `texture._needsFlipEnvMap === false;` Right?

So, as you said, the problem is to know when a cube camera render target is complete. Is that the remaining issue?

Maybe `CubeCamera.update()` can do something like this:
```js
renderTarget.texture._needsUpdate = true;
renderTarget.texture._isFromCubeCamera = true;
```
`_needsFlipEnvMap` becomes superfluous.

So the renderer will not try to create the PMREM map unless the update flag is set.

> The texture is the render target of a cube camera if texture._needsFlipEnvMap === false; Right?

When PMREM was integrated `_needsFlipEnvMap` has been removed. The replacement is `Texture.isRenderTargetTexture`.

https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/efa1b477c8430ee489eccc3559f7da634045ce74/src/textures/Texture.js#L71

`isRenderTargetTexture` is more general purpose and can be used to identify textures of render targets. I think we need to take an additional flag into account in order to identify the "ready/complete" state of a cube camera's render target.

>When PMREM was integrated _needsFlipEnvMap has been removed.

https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/efa1b477c8430ee489eccc3559f7da634045ce74/src/renderers/WebGLCubeRenderTarget.js#L40

>I think we need to take an additional flag into account in order to identify the "ready/complete" state of a cube camera's render target.

Please see my previous post.
We probably can utilize the `needsUpdate` flag of textures for this use case. I just did not have the chance yet to test it out with render targets.

@makc Opting out is not possible. `MeshPhysicalMaterial` and `MeshStandardMaterial` only support PMREM cube maps.

The only solutions are:
1. Tell the user to use `MeshPhongMaterial` instead, or
2. Tell the user to compute the PMREM manually, or
3. FIx this issue.

Another place where this breaks in a bad way is the WebXR lighting estimation API. It generates a cubemap texture for reflections of the users environment quite frequently. Obviously doing the conversion once a second will not be an acceptable solution here.

I also ran into this issue recently. I'm now generating my environment in a proper, separated way, rather than using PMREM `fromScene()`. However, I had to apply  these hacks to get the PMREM to generate: https://github.com/google/model-viewer/pull/2832/files#r730114514

@WestLangley While I agree that PMREM is a much better way to do PBR environment lighting, I think it may have been a mistake to remove the less accurate but cheaper method here: https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/22234/files#diff-7fdd1b94f9a0571f64abfb392826f21068b52acb69082c9b69bbd2a4de980a24L88

For any kind of  dynamic lighting situation, be it WebXR or something like the [cubemap dynamic example](https://threejs.org/examples/?q=dynamic#webgl_materials_cubemap_dynamic) I think it's probably worth the accuracy loss for the speedup. In fact I was trying to understand how that example still works, and my best guess is it only works for shiny materials?

I know this isn't the venue for getting help but just thought I should add it here as feedback, when I tried using `.fromScene` to use for `scene.environment` with the default parameters nothing was rendered. In the end I stuck with using a cube camera then converting it. In case there is another pitfall I have missed.
@AdaRoseCannon perhaps the default near and far plane don't fit your scene? Still, I think the plan is to deprecate that method anyway.
Just a note this has also broken the environment setting in this demo: https://threejs.org/examples/?q=light#webxr_ar_lighting
What is exactly broken in the mentioned example? It seems it looks good on desktop and mobile phone.

In AR you should see your real environment reflected in the spheres as well
as the lighting but they are just lit correctly but there is no reflection.
![Screenshot_20211018-170141_Samsung Internet Beta](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4225330/137789431-0161f176-0e47-4b68-a0cc-1249206325ca.jpg)

You're right! The environment map from `XREstimatedLight` is the texture of a `WebGLCubeRenderTarget`. And render target textures are currently not processed by the internal cubeUV conversion. 

We probably want to switch to `MeshPhongMaterial` in the example for now.

That's fine for these spheres and other ultra simple demos but it would break for even simple experiences which involve importing GLTF files since the materials there are usually standard materials and would stand out by not reflecting the environment.

Yeah. Another approach is to use `PMREMGenerator` in `SessionLightProbe` and preprocess the environment map in this component for now.

I'm still trying to figure out a solution for `WebGLRenderer`.

Or maybe we revert #22234 until this issue is solved. I tend to favor this solution for now.

The assuption of the PR (*All non-PMREM environment maps assigned to a Physical material are now converted to PMREM CubeUV format automatically by the renderer.*) is actually not true because of render targets.

The annoying thing with converting the light probe maps on the fly is that they update every ~1s depending on the system which makes gnerating them on the fly an expensive task. Perhaps it could be worth feeding back to the WebXR device API that having an option to expose them in this format directly would be a nice feature [https://github.com/immersive-web/lighting-estimation/](https://github.com/immersive-web/lighting-estimation/)

It already has some controls for other formats.

>@WestLangley While I agree that PMREM is a much better way to do PBR environment lighting, I think it may have been a mistake to remove the less accurate but cheaper method [in #22234].

Avoiding PMREM is not "less accurate"  IMO, it is completely wrong. See the comparison in https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/22178#issuecomment-887950445.

>Or maybe we revert #22234 until this issue is solved.

Please no.

@WestLangley IIRC  the main problem with those direct mip-chain methods was  having the data in the right format (RGBE won't work at all, RGBM is marginal, etc). Is there good enough support now for floating-point textures that  we could do  this in  linear space? Honestly I'd love to refactor PMREM from RGBE to  float and maybe it's time.
@elalish Regardless, I would like to see floating-point too, but @mrdoob would be the one to decide on the proper timing. Can you hack something up as a proof-of-concept?

> See the comparison in

then roll back and fix the black thing :D I wonder if all the other js engines also use pmrem or have wrong reflections

Hi hi everyone, 

If I am reading things correctly, it is true that you cannot use WebGLCubeRenderTarget's as the envMap of MeshPhysicalMaterial's?

I have configured an envMap.texture from a cubeMap render of my scene, it works great with MeshPhongMaterial, but I would love to use MeshPhysicalMaterial, so that I can blur my reflections. 

Is there a way to get this working?

@trzanko you can copy my hacks to get it working for now: https://github.com/google/model-viewer/pull/2832/files#r730114514

That will likely break once we get this fixed  properly in a new release.

@Mugen87 In model-viewer we're already using a cube camera to generate an HDR env map in `HalfFloat`; support seems to be pretty much universal now for this format. So, I believe we can now safely (I hope) switch the internal format of CubeUV from RGBE to HalfFloat, which should help performance. I believe the mip-chain alternative to PMREM deleted in #22234 will also work properly, but only with `HalfFloat` textures. 

I propose we require envMaps to be in `HalfFloat` internally (converting if necessary) and then add some kind of flag to a `CubeCamera` render target (`dynamic`?) to indicate if you want the fast path with only mipmapping for an environment that updates, or the slower, more accurate PMREM for a static environment. What do you think?

@trzanko My fix is actually just those three lines.

What do you think?

review_comments: edit: I'm assuming it should be a double-underscore.

Depending on how user or third-party code is developed both flags are actually required. 

`isRenderTargetTexture` is just the pendant to all other `is*` properties and required for type checks. Besides, users have to set `needsPMREMUpdate` to `true` (similar to other `needsUpdate` flags) if they are using a dynamic render target as an env map applied to PBR materials and author the render target's data by themselves.

I was actually thinking about suggesting something like `RenderTargetTexture` (which extends from `Texture`) in order to work a bit easier with this type of texture. However, this idea is not yet mature^^.
Okay, lets test performance in the meantime.
